newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: RTRS-Zimbabwe's Hartley mine seen on stream mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Zimbabwe's Hartley mine seen on stream mid-1997.

text.p: First metal production at Zimbabwe's largest mining investment, Hartley Platinum mine, has been set back five months to mid-June due to delays in mining and training of workers, project manager BHP Minerals said on Friday.

Hartley general manager Colin Palethorpe said the estimated cost of the project -- a joint venture between Australian mining giants Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd and Delta Gold NL -- had increased to $287 million from $264 million due to the delays.

"We have a delay to the start-up of the project, a lot of it due to the bad ground on our number one level 150 metres below surface. That has delayed the build-up of the ore stockpile. We are now looking at June 1997," Palethorpe told Reuters.
"But the biggest reason we slowed down the start-up was for safety reasons. We wanted to train everyone and there were delays in doing that," he added.
Palethorpe said about 75 percent of the 2,900 workforce had never worked in a mine and therefore needed training before going underground.

The mine -- Zimbabwe's largest direct investment since independence from Britain in 1980 -- was initially forecast to start production in November, two months ahead of schedule as construction had gone faster than scheduled.

The mine was due to reach full production of 180,000 tonnes per month of ore by next April. It now expects this with 90,000 tonnes throughput per month slotted to be reached by next September and full production by September 1998.
Palethorpe said so far an ore stockpile of 250,000 tonnes had been mined and was being put through the concentrator which started running at the end of October.
Hartley's metallurgical development manager Chris Rule said the processing plant was near completion with only the base metal refinery still to be finished.
Rule said he hoped the refinery would be completed by April next year in order for the mine to start platinum output in June.

Hartley hopes to process 2.16 million tonnes of ore per year to produce 150,000 ounces of platinum, 110,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold as well as some nickel and copper.
The mine would make Zimbabwe a major platinum producer, accounting for 3.5 percent of the world platinum market -- dominated by South Africa which produces more than 52 percent.
